culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: No rules on what visitors wear, but respectful smart-casual clothing covering shoulders to knees is appropriate at places of religious significance. A guide must accompany visitors at all times and is required to enter monuments and dzongs.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Monuments and dzongs in this dzongkhag on the official fee list: Tashichho Dzong Nu 500 (about A$7.46 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026; the ngultrum is at par with the Indian rupee) (visits 5 to 6pm, 9am to 5pm on public holidays), National Memorial Chorten Nu 500 (about A$7.46 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026; the ngultrum is at par with the Indian rupee), Changangkha Lhakhang Nu 500 (about A$7.46 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026; the ngultrum is at par with the Indian rupee), Takin preserve Nu 300 (about A$4.47 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026; the ngultrum is at par with the Indian rupee), Textile Museum and Folk Heritage Museum Nu 250 (about A$3.73 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026; the ngultrum is at par with the Indian rupee) each; Buddha Dordenma and Simtokha Dzong free.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Department of Tourism, Royal Government of Bhutan.
culture-and-protocol.note: Under-18s pay 50% and children aged five and under are free. Most monuments open 9am to 5pm. Fees are paid on arrival in cash or through the goBoB app. Conflict: an earlier search-index snapshot said Paro and Thimphu were exempt from the guide rule; the official FAQ read directly says a guide is mandatory at all times, so that is what is recorded.
